html:
The Kargil War was fought between India and Pakistan from May to July 1999 on the mountain ridges of Kargil in Kashmir. It came a year after both countries tested nuclear weapons (see the tests of 1998).

In the winter of 1998, when both armies normally left their highest posts, Pakistani soldiers crossed the Line of Control and occupied the empty Indian positions on a front of about 150 kilometres. From there they could shell the only road from Srinagar to Ladakh. Pakistan said the men were Kashmiri fighters. The plan was the army chief's, Pervez Musharraf. Only months earlier the two prime ministers had met in Lahore and promised peace.

Shepherds reported the intruders in early May. India sent about 30,000 troops and used its air force, but ordered both to stay on its own side of the line. The peaks, at 4,500 to 5,500 metres, had to be taken one by one by infantry climbing at night under fire. Tiger Hill was retaken on 4 July.

That same day the United States president told Pakistan's prime minister to pull back, and he agreed. Fighting ended on 26 July. India lost 527 soldiers; Pakistan's losses were probably higher.

In October Musharraf overthrew the prime minister. It was India's first war shown live on television.
sum: The Kargil War was fought between India and Pakistan from May to July 1999 on the mountain ridges of Kargil in Kashmir. It came a year after both countries tested nuclear weapons (see the tests of 1998).
